To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

GDNF and nerve growth factor can reverse the effect of peripheral axotomy on the kinetics of the rapidly repriming, TTX-S Na+ currents of DRG neurons, an effect which is paralleled by changes in the level of Na(v)1.
GDNF and/or NGF can reverse the effect of peripheral axotomy on the Na+ channel repriming kinetics, which are altered in a way that is consistent with an increased expression of Na(v)1,3.
the axotomy-induced changes in TTX-S current repriming in DRG neurons are reversed by intrathecal GDNF and/or NGF, and that the effect is additive.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of axotomy on Na(+) currents in DRG neurons and the ability of neurotrophic factors to reverse some of the changes in these currents that occur after axotomy.
the effects of GDNFs on the expression of TTX-S sodium channels and the repriming properties of TTX-S currents in DRG neurons.
the role of neurotrophins and their receptors in regulating neuronal excitability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GDNF and/or NGF can ameliorate changes in Na(+) channel properties of DRG neurons following peripheral axotomy.
GDNF and/or NGF can partially rescue the effect of axotomization on the reprimng of Na(+) currents in DRG neurons.
GDNF and/or NGF can partially restore axotomy-induced changes in the repriming of sodium currents in DRG neurons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
both GDN and NGF can reverse the effect of injury on the reprimng kinetics of TTX-sensitive sodium currents in DRG neurons.
the effects of axotomy on TTX-S Na+ channel repriming kinetics and Na(v)1.x transcript levels are reversed by GDNF, NGF and GDNF+NGF.
the combined administration of GDNF with NGF can prevent the majority of the changes in Na(+) channel properties and expression in axotomised DRG neurons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
GDNF and/or NGF may be useful for the treatment of chronic pain states that result from injury to sensory neurons, such as neuropathic pain.

GDNF and/or NGF can be administered together to rescue the repriming properties of TTX-S currents and that this effect may be useful in preventing the development of chronic pain following peripheral axotomy of DRG neurons.
GDNF and/or NGF could be useful in treating some chronic pain conditions that result from injury of sensory neurons.
